draft.title: Quartiles and interquartile range
card: Put the data in order from smallest to largest. The median is the middle value. It splits the data into a lower half and an upper half.
\(Q_{1}\) is the median of the lower half. When the number of values is odd, leave the overall median out of both halves.
\(Q_{3}\) is the median of the upper half. Together with the median, \(Q_{1}\) and \(Q_{3}\) split the data into four equal parts.

The interquartile range is \(\text{IQR} = Q_{3} - Q_{1}\). It is the spread of the middle half of the data. Example: for 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, the median is 7, \(Q_{1} = 4\) and \(Q_{3} = 10\), so the IQR is \(10 - 4 = 6\).
draft.remember: Order the data, find the median of each half, then subtract: \(Q_{3} - Q_{1}\).

a.q: What does the interquartile range measure?
opts: The spread of the middle half of the data
The spread from the smallest to the largest value
The average distance of values from the mean
The middle value of the ordered data
a.why: The IQR is \(Q_{3} - Q_{1}\), which covers the middle half of the data. The range is the spread from smallest to largest, which is a different measure.
a.clue: Think about which values \(Q_{1}\) and \(Q_{3}\) sit between.

b.q: Mia times her laps at a pool in Dubbo, in seconds: 31, 33, 34, 36, 38, 41, 45, 47. What is the interquartile range?
b.why: The data has 8 values, so the lower half is 31, 33, 34, 36 and \(Q_{1} = 33.5\). The upper half is 38, 41, 45, 47 and \(Q_{3} = 43\). The IQR is \(43 - 33.5 = 9.5\), not the range \(47 - 31 = 16\).
b.clue: Split the 8 values into two halves of 4 and find the median of each.
